baselines.label: Recent years
baselines.note: Every earlier year this site holds. It begins in 2015 because that is when this site starts collecting, and those years have been unusually dry, so a reservoir can look ordinary against them and still be low.

baselines.label: Standard climate period
baselines.note: The thirty year period the World Meteorological Organization defines as standard, and the same period the mountain snow measurements use. Not every reservoir existed for all of it, and each one reports how many years it has.

coverage.note: These are the reservoirs this site tracks, not all the stored water in a state.

AZ.known_additional_source: Salt River Project daily water report
AZ.note: Six reservoirs are published as a web page only, and for several of them it is the only current source.

CA.note: Read since 2026-08-20. The candidates admitted over or held behind a screen are named, with their findings, in admitted_cdec_reservoirs.json.

CO.note: Read since 2026-08-21 for the ten storage stations inside the drawn drainages. About 95 further reservoirs report on the eastern slope, whose drainages reach the Mississippi basin and are not drawn.

ID.note: The state water department points every reservoir at a federal source.

MT.known_additional_source: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers water management
MT.note: Covers the large Missouri River reservoirs. The state's own 22 dams publish no combined feed.

NM.note: The state water office publishes stream measurements rather than reservoir storage.

NV.note: No state source of reservoir storage was found. The search was not exhaustive.

OR.note: The state water department publishes no feed a program can read.

UT.note: No other public source of current storage was found.

WA.note: No independent state source was found.

WY.note: The state water service was found to republish federal readings rather than add its own.

source: Bureau of Reclamation RISE API, USDA NRCS AWDB, the California Data Exchange Center and the Colorado Division of Water Resources
